required_audit_coverage.name: required_audit_coverage
required_audit_coverage.detail: report covers all 29 Required Audit items with substantive aligned answers
required_audit_items: Is `decision_meta` present, valid, `APPROVED`, and on legal mainline `project_governance`?
Does `skill_profiles` use only active skills from `.codex-skills/registry.json`?
Does `codex_execution_report.md` match this decision ID and round ID?
Does `execution_report.md` semantically match `codex_execution_report.md`?
Does `pytest_result.txt` match this decision ID, round ID, and report ID?
Does `command_plan.json` carry current decision and round IDs?
Does command-plan authorize every executed command?
Were any omitted or unauthorized commands executed?
Does execution-log record every command-plan required command?
Does report-summary match the execution report?
Does `final_gate_result.json` pass?
Does `run_closeout_result.json` pass if closeout is permitted?
Does `workstreams.json` preserve the policy that roadmap entries are not execution authority?
Does `workstreams.json` register `project_state_domain_taxonomy` without claiming full implementation completion?
Does the normal-pace roadmap document exist and avoid rushed MVP commitments?
Does the state taxonomy supplement document exist and distinguish Phase A from future migration phases?
Does `state_manifest.json` include or support role/scope/domain/mainline/freshness metadata for state files?
Does `artifact_index.json` include or support scope/domain/mainline/freshness metadata for artifact entries?
Does `negative_results.json` include or support global/domain scope metadata while preserving legacy compatibility?
Do tests cover legacy records without metadata and new scoped records with metadata?
Does final-check/report-summary surface scoped metadata coverage without hard-failing old records in this phase?

Did the implementation avoid modifying `current_state.json`, `task_packet.json`, `project_state/domains/*`, `.codex-skills/*`, `.github/workflows/*`, `frontend/*`, `solve_reports/*`, and database files?

Did the implementation avoid Web/frontend runtime, runner dispatch, workflow dispatch, model API invocation, database writes, cleanup apply, file deletion/move, sample solving, and external reverse tools?
Did this round reuse existing state_manifest/artifact_index/negative_results/project_gate/report mechanisms rather than creating parallel systems?
Does the final conclusion avoid claiming completion of future domain migration phases?
`ACCEPTED`
`ACCEPTED_WITH_LIMITATIONS`
`REWORK_REQUIRED`
`BLOCKED`
